ny_mud_pond.blurb: Mud Pond is a backwoods cliff in the Silver Lake area of the Adirondacks, set off to the southeast of the other crags there. Around twenty routes, nearly all trad with a couple of bolted lines, climb clean white and pink rock that is steep in places and cut by corners, arêtes and cracks. Easy climbs are scarce: grades fall mostly from 5.9 through 5.11, in roughly equal shares, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on sustained crack and corner climbing. The wall bends around, so one end warms up early and the other later in the day. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons; biting insects can be heavy in between. The walk in follows old logging roads.
ny_mud_pond.parking_note: Leave the car at a logging road a short distance before the Silver Lake Mountain trailhead, roughly a fifth of a mile; the same pull-off is used for the neighbouring cliffs.

ny_boxcar_area.blurb: Boxcar Area is a bouldering zone at the far northern end of the Trapps in the Gunks, along the carriage road beneath the big cliff, on hard quartz conglomerate. It holds about twenty problems and makes a full day for a small group. Most are on the easier side, roughly three quarters falling between V0 and V2, with a few in the middle grades and a small group of much harder lines at V8 and above, so beginners and strong boulderers can both find something. The walk from the Trapps bridge is a fair stroll, and the main boulder is easy to spot from the road.

ny_9_jersey_volunteers.blurb: Jersey Volunteers is a southeast-facing slab in the Powerlinez climbing area of Harriman State Park, near Ramapo. It carries about twenty short routes, mostly top-rope with a few trad lines, ranging from easy terrain up to 5.10b, with the largest cluster in the 5.10 range. The slab is among the sparsest in the area for positive holds, with long smooth stretches and a low roof, so it rewards balance and footwork. Protection for leading is thin, which is why top-roping dominates. It is one of the quickest crags to reach from the main trailhead, making it a handy warm-up or a stop on a day around the east end.
ny_9_jersey_volunteers.approach: From the main trailhead, follow the dirt road north about a quarter mile to the junction near the electrical substation. Bear sharply left onto a second dirt road and walk southwest roughly 50 m, then leave the road to the right and push uphill northwest about 50 m to the foot of the slab.

ny_big_boy_boulder.blurb: Big Boy Boulder is the largest block at East Marion on Long Island's North Fork, sitting on the beach and often described as the island's signature boulder. Roughly twenty problems cover a range of angles and styles on granite. Moderate climbs from V1 to V3 are present, but the bulk of the problems are harder, with a cluster around V8 and V9 and one at V11, so it appeals most to climbers working in the upper grades. Being a beach site, tides and wind shape the visit, so check the water level and weather before you go.
ny_big_boy_boulder.parking_note: Reach East Marion on Route 25, then follow Rocky Point Road north to its end, where a small lot sits above a long staircase down to the beach.
ny_big_boy_boulder.approach: Go down the long staircase to the beach and walk west along the shore. This is the farthest-west boulder in the cluster.

nl_spanky_s_playground.blurb: Spanky's Playground is a compact seaside crag at Flatrock on the Avalon Peninsula, north of St. John's. The cliffs are short but pack in about twenty-six routes, a mix of trad (the larger share) and bolted sport lines, on the conglomerate typical of the area. Grades run from an easy 5.4 to the low 5.13s, with the heart of it at 5.9 through 5.11, so there is enough for a range of abilities. Because it faces the ocean it stays cool on hot days, but the middle section catches the most spray and the rock can turn slick and green in wet spells. Rough seas make the base a poor place to be.

nl_the_after_hours.blurb: The After-Hours is a small, well-sheltered pocket of granite on remote Fair Island, off Newfoundland's northeast coast. Of its twenty-one climbs, sixteen are boulder problems, mostly in the easiest range from VB to V3, and the other five are trad lines spanning about 5.7 to 5.11. The granite is good and solid but sharp on the skin, so tape and fresh skin matter. Shade and breeze shift with the weather and time of day. The place is quiet and isolated, and the walk in crosses marsh, brush and rocky shoreline before a steep drop into the area.
